scenicLandscapes|p0006.why: Peak cut from 10 to 9.8: Antarctica is not on the Scenic list of places allowed a 10, so you decide whether it should be (the polar-ice rating is 10, iconic view 9). Gemini said the closed months were polar darkness; the Peninsula does not have polar night, so now it is sea ice and storms with no passenger ships. November, December to February and March each have their own blurb (Gemini grouped November with March). Ship logs show the Lemaire Channel is blocked by ice on some voyages and passable on others in any month, so the text says 'often passable' and 'may be out of reach' instead of 'usually clear'.

scenicLandscapes|p0043.why: Left as Gemini wrote it: peak 4.6, the skyline from the lake and river, with boat tours as the way to see it. Below the Paris-style 5.5 to 6 because the lakefront is the only view and winter is harsh.

scenicLandscapes|p0057.why: On the Scenic list of places allowed a 10, so July stays 10. July and August are separate from June and September (all lifts open versus a few snowy high routes). The lift claims were checked: the Alpe di Siusi lifts open from late May and run to about 1 November, so the text says 'some cable cars' rather than 'many'. Larch woods turning gold in October is well known, but I did not find a source that gives dates.

scenicLandscapes|p0162.why: Peak cut from 10 to 9.7: Santorini is not on the Scenic list of places allowed a 10, so you decide. Removed 'offer'. The winter blurb is a shallow trough (7.0 to 7.5) kept as one group because a winter dip is what a reader expects.

scenicLandscapes|p0191.why: Gemini gave a flat 6.5 and a blurb saying the views are 'visible in every season', which is filler; it now says what changes (fog and high water in the cooler months, clear days in summer). Venice is a city where the setting is the view, so 6.5 may be low (the Paris rule is 5.5 to 6); your call on a rank check.

stargazing|p0035.why: Rebuilt the grouping: Gemini put March, April and September together and used the phrase 'true darkness' and quoted hours of darkness. Now four contiguous blurbs (long nights with the core down, core rising before dawn, shortest nights with the core overhead, core fading in the evening). No hours quoted. 'Premier' removed. The fact sheet's 'dry months' line for the Canaries lists all twelve months, which is useless; I ignored it.

stargazing|p0069.why: Gemini put March into a September-to-October group and said 'midnight sun'. Facts: no astronomical darkness at all from April to August, so the first blurb says the sky never gets fully dark and few stars show. Separate blurbs for September to October (darkness back, cloud), November to December (cloudiest, core below the horizon) and January to March (long nights, thinner cloud, the best months). Peak 5.5 is low next to Atacama because cloud is 67 to 93% at night; Bortle 3 gives dark skies when it clears.

stargazing|p0114.why: A 10 for Namibia is allowed (it is on the Stargazing list). NamibRand is an IDA-certified dark-sky reserve. 'Winter' replaced by months because Namibia is in the southern hemisphere. 'Premier' removed.

stargazing|p0170.why: Peak 2.6: Bortle 7, cloud 79 to 98% at night. I removed the named parks Gemini listed as 'darker spots' (they are not meaningfully dark), and the moon. October lowered to 1.2 so the wet-season group is a smooth trough.

stargazing|p0159.why: Gemini said the water 'sometimes reflects' the sky in a general way; now it is tied to the wet-season film of water that mirrors the stars. Core visibility checked against the sky: core rises after midnight in April and May, is overhead June to August, and is only up in the first half of the night in September and October. Peak 9.9 (a 10 is allowed).

sunbathing|p0002.why: Gemini's May-and-October blurb said 'less reliable than in summer', which names a season for non-neighbor months; removed. Temperatures match the climate table (July and August 85, June and September 80, May and October 74). Winter score floor 0.8 to 1.6.

sunbathing|p0083.why: Left as Gemini wrote it (0.9 peak). The only sunbathing is on black-sand beaches in summer highs of the upper 50s.

sunbathing|p0165.why: Temperatures corrected to the climate table (May 84, June 94, September 89, October 79 give 'upper 70s to mid 90s'; July 97 and August 94 give 'mid to upper 90s'). Peak 7.5 is below the 8.5 to 9 ceiling because there is no beach and the only draw is resort pools.

spaWellness|p0030.why: Flat 9.8 all year. 'Premier' and 'offers' removed. The Roman-Irish baths exist in Baden-Baden (Friedrichsbad and Caracalla). Mixed nude saunas are the German custom, so the overview calls that out, as you asked for unusual customs. The outdoor thermal pools stay warm in winter, so snow adds to the soak.

spaWellness|p0080.why: Gemini grouped April to November as one blurb with scores 0.6 apart; now April to September, October to November and December to March each have a blurb. spaWellness|p0085.why: Gemini gave a flat 10. spaWellness|p0087.why: On the Spa 10 list. Removed 'deep-tissue' (Ayurvedic treatments are oil massage, not deep-tissue). The monsoon being the traditional season for the long treatments is the real Ayurvedic custom, kept. April and May both 8.9 so the drier-months group is a smooth fall.

spaWellness|p0166.why: Left as Gemini wrote it: it already calls out the jjimjilbang custom (nude gender-separated baths, mixed saunas in provided uniforms, body scrubs by attendants).
